question: Which initiative differs from the others in terms of sectoral focus?
solution:
The correct answer is __**PM Fasal Bima Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **PM Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** focuses on the **agriculture sector** and aims to provide **financial support to farmers** in case of crop failures due to natural calamities, pests, or diseases.
 
• It is a unique initiative compared to the other options, as it is **sector-specific** to agriculture and rural farmers, while the other initiatives focus on logistics, infrastructure, or governance systems.
 
• The scheme was **launched in 2016** by the Government of India to ensure risk coverage and stability for farmers.
 
• PMFBY provides **insurance coverage** and encourages farmers to adopt modern practices, ensuring long-term agricultural growth and sustainability.
 
• All other options such as the **National Single Window System, Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS),** and **PM Gati Shakti** are initiatives focused on **logistics and infrastructure** development, making PMFBY distinct in its purpose.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Single Window System (NSWS):**

 
 
• The **NSWS** is an initiative by the Government of India to provide a **one-stop digital platform** for investors and businesses to access clearances and approvals.
 
• It focuses on **ease of doing business** and integrates several central and state government services into a unified interface.
 
• The aim is to improve the investment climate and attract both domestic and foreign investments.
 
 
 
• **Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS):**
 
 
• The **LEADS Index** is a survey-based assessment that ranks states based on their logistics ecosystem.
 
• It is aimed at improving the **efficiency of logistics services** and ensuring better infrastructure and processes to facilitate trade and economic growth.
 
 
 
• **PM Gati Shakti:**
 
 
• It is a **national master plan** for multi-modal connectivity to bring synergy among different infrastructure sectors in India.
 
• The initiative focuses on **efficient project planning and execution** to ensure cost and time savings in large-scale infrastructure development.
 
• PM Gati Shakti aims to **connect economic zones** and improve the logistics ecosystem of the country.
 
 
 
• **PM Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):**
 
 
• Launched in **2016**, PMFBY provides **crop insurance** to farmers to protect against unforeseen losses due to natural disasters, pests, and diseases.
 
• Farmers are required to pay a minimal premium, and the government pays the balance premium to the insurance company.
 
• This scheme is vital for the **socio-economic stability** of farmers and enhances their resilience to climate and market risks.
 
• It is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare in collaboration with state governments and insurance companies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Coverage under PMFBY:**

 
 
• The scheme covers **pre-sowing to post-harvest losses** for notified crops across different regions of India.
 
• The **premium rates** for farmers are kept at **2% for Kharif crops**, **1.5% for Rabi crops**, and **5% for commercial/horticultural crops**.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of PMFBY:**
 
 
• Since its inception, PMFBY has provided substantial **financial relief** to farmers during natural disasters and has covered millions of hectares of farmland.
 
• The scheme has encouraged the adoption of **scientific farming techniques** and improved productivity in the agricultural sector.
 
 
 
• **Distinction from other schemes:**
 
 
• While other initiatives like LEADS and Gati Shakti focus on logistics and infrastructure, PMFBY is uniquely targeted toward **agricultural risk management** and farmer welfare.
